name: ANSI NAND gate drawn as negative-input OR
summary: OR outline with bubbles on its inputs: the De Morgan form of a NAND used when inputs are active low.
description: By De Morgan's theorem, a NAND gate is equivalent to an OR gate whose inputs are inverted. Data books and well-drawn schematics use the OR outline with input bubbles when the inputs are active-low signals, so that the drawing reads as any of these low signals produces a high output.

This form is useful where active-low requests or fault lines are combined. Matching bubbles to active-low nets lets a reader follow the logic without mentally inverting each signal, which is the main reason for choosing this representation.
The symbol represents the same physical part as the conventional NAND outline. It does not mean an OR device and inverters are fitted, and the bill of materials will still list a NAND package.
readingNotes: Recognise bubbled inputs on an OR outline as a NAND device.
Expect the input nets to be active-low signals.
drawingChecklist: Use this form when the input signals are active low.
Keep the device reference the same as the NAND package.
Explain the convention in the sheet legend for unfamiliar readers.
distinction: An OR outline with a bubble at the output is a NOR, not this NAND equivalent.
